'''''Brugmansia sanguinea''''', the '''red angel's trumpet''', is a species of South American flowering shrub or small tree belonging to the genus Brugmansia in tribe [[Datureae]] of subfamily [[Solanoideae]] of the nightshade family ''[[Solanaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:814612-1 |title= Brugmansia sanguinea (Ruiz & Pav.) D.Don |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=February 1, 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/NFDD |title= Brugmansia sanguinea (Ruiz & Pav.) D.Don |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=February 1, 2025}}</ref> It has been cultivated and used as an [[entheogen]] for [[shaman]]ic purposes by the South American Natives for centuries - possibly even millennia.<ref>Hoffmann, Albert; Schultes Richard Evans; Ratsch, Christian; Plants of the Gods, pp. 33</ref>

==Description==
''Brugmansia sanguinea'' is a small tree reaching up to {{convert|10|m|abbr=on}} in height. The  pendent, tubular/trumpet-shaped flowers come in shades of brilliant red, yellow, orange and green.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Cullen|first1=James|last2=Knees|first2=Sabina G.|last3=Cubey|first3=Suzanne|title=The European Garden Flora: Volume 5, Dicotyledons: Boraginaceae to Compositae|year=2011|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-76164-2|page=266|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KLPcml_QiFQC&q=brugmansia%20sanguinea&pg=PA142}}</ref>

==Distribution==
''B. sanguinea'' is [[Endemism|endemic]] to the [[Andes]] mountains from [[Colombia]] to northern [[Chile]] at elevations from {{convert|2000|to|3000|m|abbr=on}}.<ref name='Preissel'>{{cite book | last1 = Preissel | first1 = Ulrike | last2 = Preissel | first2 = Hans-Georg | title = Brugmansia and Datura: Angel's Trumpets and Thorn Apples | publisher = Firefly Books | year = 2002 | location = Buffalo, New York | pages = 106–129 | isbn = 1-55209-598-3 }}</ref>

==Toxicity==
{{Main|Brugmansia#Toxicity|l1=Brugmansia (Toxicity)}}
All parts of ''Brugmansia sanguinea'' are poisonous. Different parts of the plant contain [[tropane alkaloid]]s in varying proportions. Alkaloid content in the flowers is mainly atropine with only traces of scopolamine ([[hyoscine]]).<ref name="Encyclopedia of Shamanism">{{cite book|last=Pratt|first=Christina|title=An Encyclopedia of Shamanism Volume 1|year=2007|publisher=The Rosen Publishing Group|isbn=978-1-4042-1140-7|pages=68–70|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=V_betetLgEMC&q=brugmansia&pg=PA69}}</ref><ref name="plants of the gods p37"/> The seeds of ''B. sanguinea'' contain approximately 0.17% alkaloids by mass, of which 78% are scopolomine.<ref name="plants of the gods p37">{{cite book |title=Plants of the Gods  |author1=Hoffmann, Albert |author2=Schultes, Richard Evans |author3=Ratsch, Christian |page=37 |url=https://www.scribd.com/doc/35522979/Plants-of-the-Gods-Their-Sacred-Healing-and-Hallucinogenic-Powers-2e-R-E-Schultes-A-Hofmann-C-Ratsch-2001-0892819790 |access-date=9 February 2019}}</ref>
